rows.subtype: After this, therefore because of this [Actor]
rows.description: A child thinks the rain came because he did a dance or that he got fever because he ate ice cream once. Something that follows an event seems caused by it.

rows.description: A teenager credits a tonic, a lucky charm or an app for recovering or scoring well, when things might have improved by themselves anyway.

rows.description: A student receives forwarded messages claiming a herb cured someone right after taking it. The timing sounds convincing but ignores natural recovery and other causes.

rows.description: A wise person asks what would have happened without the treatment or change, looks for repeated and controlled evidence, and sees a doctor for real health problems.

rows.description: A child assumes all friends like the same food, game and film he does, and is surprised or hurt when they differ. He believes his tastes are normal for all.
